subject.title: Bug: Poe image/video-output models are accepted in config but fail at runtime (Nano Banana 400, Veo/Sora fallback)

question: Should OpenClaw treat image/video-output provider model refs as unsupported chat/session models with clear diagnostics, or add a first-class output-modality contract that routes those refs through media generation?
rationale: Both paths change public provider/model semantics: diagnostics need a way to identify output-only models, while first-class support requires broader provider, tool, response, and channel contracts.

options.title: Diagnostic-first contract
options.body: Add or derive enough output-modality metadata to fail fast for media-output chat/session selections while leaving generation on image_generate and video_generate.

options.title: First-class media-output models
options.body: Add output modality metadata and route image/video-output model refs through media generation runtime with channel delivery support.

options.title: Wait for plugin proof
options.body: Keep core unchanged until a Poe or generic media provider plugin proves the missing API surface and desired user workflow.

recommendation.title: Diagnostic-first contract
recommendation.body: Add or derive enough output-modality metadata to fail fast for media-output chat/session selections while leaving generation on image_generate and video_generate.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans provider contracts, model catalog semantics, and media generation routing, where the history points most strongly to steipete as the available product/API owner.
